news.title: FIFPro, UEFA Demand Independent Review of FIFA FFE Plan
news.lede: Fifpro and Fifpro Europe backed UEFA’s call for an independent review of FIFA’s scrapped Forward Enterprise plan, which sought private investment in World Cup commercial operations. A $20 billion valuation assigned to FIFA’s Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal has intensified scrutiny over the governing body’s decision-making process, prompting Fifpro and Fifpro Europe to formally support an independent review on Monday. Under the FFE scheme, private investors would have acquired a 20 per cent stake in a business entity responsible for managing commercial operations across FIFA events — including both the men’s and women’s World Cups. The project was abandoned after three continental confederations rejected it, with UEFA threatening to boycott FIFA tournaments unless the plan was withdrawn and assurances given against any future recurrence.

news.title: Christian Tsangas named in Pararoos squad for IFCPF Men’s World Cup 2026
news.lede: Football Australia has confirmed the 14-player CommBank Pararoos squad that will represent Australia at the IFCPF Men’s World Cup 2026 in Atlanta, USA from 12-24 October. Head Coach Kai Lammert’s squad features significant World Cup experience, with 11 players returning from the group that represented Australia at the 2024 edition in Salou, Spain. The squad also includes first-time Pararoo Josh De Silva (Football West), whose journey back to football following an acquired brain injury has culminated in his maiden national team selection. The squad features players from five Member Federations across Australia, with five representatives from Football NSW, four from Football West, three from Football Victoria, and one each from Football Queensland and Capital Football.

news.title: Saudi football authorities launch disciplinary proceedings over offensive chants about Diogo Jota
news.lede: ISTANBUL, Sept 15 — The Saudi Arabian Football Federation (SAFF) and Saudi Professional League condemned chants directed at late Liverpool and Portugal forward Diogo Jota during a Saturday match between Al-Taawoun and Al-Hilal, vowing disciplinary action against those responsible. In a joint statement late Sunday, the SAFF and the league called the behaviour during the Saudi Professional League match “unacceptable” and contrary to the values of Saudi football and sportsmanship, Anadolu Ajansi reported. The governing bodies said exploiting personal tragedies to incite or provoke others “has no place in Saudi football.” The SAFF said relevant committees had monitored the incidents and initiated disciplinary proceedings in line with established regulations and bylaws.

news.title: Three new names in All Whites football squad
news.lede: Three uncapped players have been included in Darren Bazeley's first All Whites squad named following June’s FIFA World Cup. Teenage forward Stipe Ukich, 26-year-old centre back George Stanger and 21-year-old goalkeeper Henry Gray are in line to make their debuts when the team heads to Asia for four matches in the international window that starts next week. Nix men recruit Scottish midfielder. Ukich, 19 has played for New Zealand at various junior levels and currently competes in the Croatian top league for NK Istra 1961.

news.title: Malawi’s Women Made World Cup History. Can That Attention Turn Into Arrivals?
news.lede: Temwa Chawinga was already one of the biggest names in American women’s soccer before this summer. The Kansas City Current forward has won the NWSL Golden Boot and MVP award in back-to-back seasons, becoming the first player in league history to win consecutive MVP titles. Her older sister, Tabitha, captains Malawi and plays for OL Lyonnes after a career that has taken her through Sweden, China, Milan, and Paris. This summer, what changed was the national team around them.

news.title: Justin Bieber, Shakira, BTS and Madonna will not be paid for World Cup final half time show
news.lede: The halftime show might also break FIFA's own rules. Much like at the Super Bowl, the headliners at the World Cup final halftime show will not be paid for their performances - but for a different reason. Justin Bieber, Shakira, Madonna, Burna Boy, and BTS are among the huge names performing in the 11-minute show in front of tens of thousands of fans at the MetLife Stadium, as well as being broadcast to millions around the world. The final is scheduled for 19 July, with the halftime show being the first such performance to happen at a FIFA World Cup, being curated by Coldplay's Chris Martin.

news.title: 'Total mess' - LaLiga club set for 70,000 World Cup stadium could be relegated
news.lede: That's according to European football journalists Kevin Hatchard and Andy Brassell as they sit winless at the bottom of Spain's top flight. After their 1-0 defeat to Sevilla on Friday night, Valencia have just one point to show for their efforts with five matches played in LaLiga. Carlos Corberan, formerly in charge of Championship side West Brom, has been sacked as head coach of his boyhood club amid their poor run. Ex-Chelsea chief Ron Gourlay has also been dismissed from his role as CEO of Football at Valencia, who were crowned Spanish champions in the 2003/04 season.
